title: Diplomacy across the water
paragraphs: Baekje’s political world extended beyond peninsular neighbors. Communication across the Yellow Sea and toward the Japanese archipelago formed part of wider patterns of exchange. Diplomatic contacts could carry gifts, prestige objects, religious ideas, specialized knowledge, and claims about the status of rulers. Such movement was neither identical to conquest nor neatly separated from it.

The relationship between archaeology and later written traditions remains important here. Similar objects found in distant places indicate connections, but they do not by themselves identify the precise political arrangement behind those connections. A careful account leaves room for movement that did not pass through a single central authority.
